lockup.summary: The company, its directors and officers, and holders of nearly all its stock cannot sell for at least 180 days after the prospectus date. Goldman Sachs and Jefferies can give written consent to sell sooner, with some exceptions.

what: It develops RNA interference medicines meant to switch off disease-causing proteins. Its drug candidates are in or heading into clinical trials.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about $181.5 million. It plans to spend about $30.0 million on CITY-FXI, $20.0 million on CITY-RBP4, $40.0 million on CITY-TFR2 and $70.0 million on its City Platform. The rest goes to working capital and general costs.
risks: It is an early-stage drug developer with a short history and no approved products, so its future is hard to judge.
It has never earned revenue from selling drugs, and becoming profitable depends on many factors.
Its approach to finding and making new medicines is new and may never produce products that can be sold.
Its work centers on RNAi technology, so its success depends on this technology and on its City Platform working.
It may lack the money to keep developing a drug if problems delay or block approval or sale.
